title: Deployment and modern trends
subtitle: Getting code from a laptop to users, repeatably and safely.

sections.title: Environments
sections.body: Code moves through environments: development (your machine), staging (a production-like copy for final checks), production (real users). Configuration (URLs, secrets) comes from environment variables, never committed to the repository — the same build runs everywhere.

sections.title: CI/CD pipeline
sections.body: Every push triggers: install → lint → test → build → deploy to staging → (approval) → deploy to production. A failing stage stops the line. Automated pipelines make releases boring.

choices.text: To catch problems in a production-like place before users see them.

figures.note: The token moves on only when the stage passes.

sections.title: Containers
sections.body: A container (Docker) packages an app with its dependencies, so “works on my machine” means works everywhere. An image is the recipe; a container is a running instance. Kubernetes schedules, scales and heals containers across machines.

questions.prompt: A Docker image is to a container as…

choices.text: An object is to a class.
A class is to an object.
A file is to a folder.

sections.title: Safe release strategies
sections.body: Blue–green: run old (blue) and new (green) side by side, switch traffic, switch back if broken. Canary: send 5 % of traffic to the new version first. Feature flags ship code turned off. Always have a fast rollback.

worked.why: A bug affects 2 % of requests. A 5 % canary sees it on:

questions.prompt: A canary release reduces risk by…

figures.caption: Figure 6.4.1 — canary release
figures.note: Promote only while the canary looks healthy.

problems.prompt: A canary takes 10 % of traffic and the bug hits 3 % of requests. What share of all traffic is affected?

sections.title: Performance and caching
sections.body: Minify and compress (gzip/brotli), cache static files with long max-age and hashed names, serve from a CDN near the user, lazy-load images, avoid render-blocking scripts. Measure with Core Web Vitals: LCP (loading), INP (responsiveness), CLS (layout stability).

questions.prompt: A CDN speeds up a site mainly by…

choices.text: Serving files from a location near the user.

sections.title: Modern trends
sections.body: Serverless functions (pay per call), edge computing, server-side rendering with hydration, Progressive Web Apps (installable, offline), WebAssembly for near-native speed, WebSockets/SSE for real-time updates, and AI-assisted development. Pick the simplest architecture that meets the need.

choices.text: You deploy functions; the provider runs and scales servers.

responses.title: Correct.
responses.body: Servers still exist, but are not yours to manage.
